correctness.rationale: For each admissible edge (i,j), the vertex chart is generated by (u_p/u_i)(v_q/v_j) over allowed edges. Write H=m+1-j and L=m+1-i. If p>H, each allowed partner satisfies q<j; with the column generators for q<j these monomials form C_{j-1}. If q>L, the analogous monomials with p<i give C_{i-1}. For p<=H and q<=L the individual ratios occur from edges incident to i or j, and their products add no generators. The remaining ratios give 2(m+1-i-j) free variables. The three blocks use disjoint sets of algebraically independent ratios, so the rings tensor over C and the coordinate point maps to their product origin. Grading each cone by the exponent sum on its b-variables puts every primitive generator in degree one; the origin ideal's associated graded (also after localization) is then the standard graded tensor product. Corso–Nagel Example 5.11 at shape (t+1,...,2) gives the stated single-cone series; t=0 is a point, t=1 is a polynomial ring in two generators. Tensor product gives denominator dimension 2m-2 and the product of Narayana numerators. The primitive generator count in C_t is t(t+3)/2, giving tangent excess t(t-1)/2. Thus precisely (1,1),(1,2),(2,1),(2,2) are smooth for m>=3. Concatenation embeds pairs of Dyck paths into those of total semilength and misses primitive Dyck paths when both lengths are positive. Together with strict Catalan growth from index 1 and m-1>=2, this gives exactly the two stated extremal maximizers. My independent exponent-sum calculation directly counted chart Hilbert function terms at all 52 charts for 3<=m<=6 through degree 3 and matched the formula, including the degree-one tangent counts. Replay with python3 /workspace/branches/independent_checks.py 3. The frozen checker and its recorded run were inspected, not executed; the finite checks corroborate and do not replace the all-m argument.

value.rationale: Knowing singularity support or the global Ferrers Hilbert series is not enough to recover a fixed-point local ring. The affine product theorem gives the local rings by explicit coordinates for a natural family and makes their complete local Hilbert functions and multiplicity comparison uniform, including where different cone factors contribute. This is structural information beyond a list of singular points or recomputed Catalan numbers.
